transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Um… I guess what brings me in is that lately I feel like I just can’t really settle in my own body. It’s not all the time, or maybe I try not to make a big deal of it, but especially when I’m supposed to sit quietly and do paperwork or talk through household plans with someone, I get this restless feeling like I need to get up or do something. I’m not sure if that makes sense.
Have you started or changed the dose of any medications recently, especially antipsychotics, antiemetics, or other prescription drugs?

Um… I don’t think so. Not that I can think of, anyway. I’m not on anything like that, or I haven’t recently started or changed a dose. If there’s a specific kind of medication you mean, I can try to remember, but I don’t think there’s been anything new.
When you feel this restlessness, do you also notice a lot of worrying thoughts running through your mind, or is it mainly just a physical urge to move without particular worries attached?

I mean, I do worry sometimes, sure, but with this thing it feels more like… my body just won’t settle. Like when I’m supposed to sit and do paperwork or talk through household plans, I get this uncomfortable urge to move or get up. It’s not necessarily that I’m panicking about something specific. Is that the kind of distinction you mean?
Thinking back, has this kind of restlessness and difficulty sitting still been something you've noticed since childhood or your teenage years, or is this a new pattern that started more recently?

I think it’s been there a long time, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was—I did okay in school—but even in elementary school I was sort of known for having a messy desk and losing things, like permission slips. And I remember teachers writing notes that I talked when I wasn’t supposed to, or that I had trouble staying in my seat. So… I guess it’s not totally new, if that’s what you’re asking.
Aside from the restlessness, do you often find it hard to stay focused on tasks, make careless mistakes, or forget things you were supposed to do—both now and back when you were a kid?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, because I can focus sometimes. But yes, it happens enough that I notice it. Like I’ll sit down with a planning email or even a chapter of a book, and I start out thinking I’m reading it properly, but after a few minutes I realize I’m just staring at the same paragraph and none of it actually went in.

I remember some version of that when I was younger too, though I probably didn’t have the words for it then. Does that make sense?
Do you often find yourself interrupting others, blurting out responses before someone finishes speaking, or having trouble waiting your turn in conversations or lines?

I try really hard not to, because I do care about being respectful. But… yes, I think I do that more than I’d like to admit. Especially with my husband, I’ll jump into his conversations or finish what I think he’s about to say, and sometimes the response is just out before I’ve made myself wait.

It’s not that I mean to be rude. I usually realize right after and feel bad about it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Would you say these attention and restlessness issues have caused noticeable problems in more than one area of your life—like both at home and at work or in social situations?

Yes… I think so. I hate saying that because I really do try, and I don’t want it to sound like I just don’t care or I’m unreliable on purpose.

But at home, and also with volunteer things I’m involved in, there’s been fallout. People can’t always count on me the way I want them to, because I’ll let something slip or not follow through even when I meant to. I’ve actually had to step back from some responsibilities because I kept dropping the ball. It’s embarrassing, but… yes, it’s more than one area.

Thinking back to before you turned 12 years old, do you recall these same kinds of symptoms—like trouble staying seated, losing things, or blurting things out—actually causing noticeable problems for you at that age?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I was a pretty good kid, so I don’t want to make it sound like I was constantly in trouble, but looking back, it was already there in elementary school.

I was the girl with the messy desk, the permission slips I forgot to turn in, that kind of thing. And I do remember teacher notes saying I talked out of turn or couldn’t seem to stay seated. At the time I think people just saw it as me being chatty or disorganized, maybe, but it did cause problems. Does that answer what you’re asking?
